title: Eating disorder risk and sexual victimization: considering the impact of LGBTQ+ status
abstract: A limited body of research has linked eating disorders (EDs) with sexual victimization (SV) among college students. This research highlights higher ED risks for females, but how gender relates to EDs and SV among LGBTQ+ individuals remains underexplored. Specifically, there is minimal research on the experiences of transgender, gender non-conforming and sexual minority students who experience EDs and SV compared to their cisgender classmates. We examine whether LGBTQ+ students who have been sexually victimized are at greater risk for EDs using data from the spring 2021 National College Health Assessment. Our findings indicate that EDs are more prevalent among sexual and gender minority college students than their cisgender, heterosexual peers and that SV is associated with an increased likelihood of having an ED. However, SV did not differentially impact ED risk among sexual or gender minorities, though the predicted probability of EDs is highest for sexual and gender minorities who have experienced SV. Institutions of higher learning may benefit from culturally sensitive ED prevention and response programmes that also address the overlapping needs of students affected by SV, particularly among sexual and gender minorities.
